name: von Laue's theorem (1911): volume integral of spatial stress of a static closed system is a surface term / vanishes

source.located: M. Laue, 'Zur Dynamik der Relativitaetstheorie', Ann. Phys. (Leipzig) 1911 -- printed as 'Ann. Phys. 35, 524 (1911)' by Wang and as 'Annalen Phys. 340, 524 (1911)' by Lorce et al. 2109.11785 ref [30] and Pinto & Avelino 2502.10427 ref [32]. No arXiv copy; the 1911 paper itself was NOT read.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries, page text: C. Wang arXiv:1206.5618v12 = Can. J. Phys. 93, 1470 (2015), pp.1-7 (theorem statement sec.2, fn.7, secs.4-6, eq.(20)); Lorce, Metz, Pasquini & Rodini arXiv:2109.11785 pp.1-5,7-8,11-12 (eqs.(14),(15),(18),(19),(23),(65)); Sorge arXiv:2011.10991 pp.1-13 (assumption (a), eqs.(31)-(36)); Pinto & Avelino arXiv:2502.10427v2 pp.1-3,5-9 (eqs.(22)-(27),(39)-(43)). Von Laue 1911 is NAMED-NOT-READ; Giulini arXiv:1808.09320 (the modern derivation Pinto-Avelino follow) NAMED-NOT-READ.

published_statement: As restated by Wang (1206.5618, p.2): 'Assume that Theta^{mu nu}(x) is a Lorentz four-tensor given in the laboratory frame ... Theta is independent of time (dTheta/dt = 0), and further Theta^{i4}(x) = 0 ... von Laue's theorem [1] states: The time-row-element space integrals P^mu = int_V Theta^{mu 4} d^3x ... constitute a Lorentz four-vector if and only if int_V Theta^{ij} d^3x = 0 (2).' Wang fn.7: 'In the original ref. 1, Laue only gave the proof that int Theta^{ij} d^3x = 0 is a sufficient condition.' The finite-volume relation the tree cites is Wang sec.6 eq.(20): 'With dTheta/dt = 0 ... from the three-dimensional Gauss divergence law we have oint_S dS_l (Theta^{l mu} X^i) = int_V (d_l Theta^{l mu}) X^i d^3x + int_V Theta^{i mu} d^3x' and Wang p.5: 'the divergence-less property plus an additional boundary condition can be a sufficient condition ... Suppose that the boundary condition oint_S dS_l Theta^{l mu} X^i = 0 holds, which is true if Theta^{mu nu}(x) = 0 is imposed on the boundary'; and 'divergence-less (itself) is neither a necessary condition nor a sufficient condition'. The vanishing form as the modern literature states it (Pinto & Avelino 2502.10427 eqs.(24)-(25), following Giulini): 'int_Sigma T^{mu j} delta^i_j d^3x = int_dSigma T^{mu j} x^i n_j dS ... If T^{mu j} = 0 at dSigma or if Sigma represents the whole fixed time hyperplane and T^{mu j} decays sufficiently fast (e.g. T ~ 1/r^{3+eps}) then int_Sigma T^{mu i} d^3x = 0'; Lorce et al. eq.(15): 'the von Laue condition for mechanical equilibrium int d^3x p(x) = 0' for a closed system (conserved total EMT), 'we will drop all surface terms, assuming as usual that their contributions vanish'.
published_hypotheses: static: dTheta^{mu nu}/dt = 0 in the frame considered (Wang sec.2, emphasised p.3)
Theta^{i4} = 0 (no momentum density) for the classical four-vector form (Wang sec.2)
closed system: the TOTAL stress-energy tensor is divergence-free, no external force density (Lorce eq.(14)/(19); with a force F, int T^{ij} = -int x^i F^j, Lorce eq.(18))

boundary condition: T^{l mu} = 0 on the bounding surface (Wang p.5; Pinto-Avelino eq.(25); Sorge assumption (a) 'T vanishing outside Omega' and eq.(35) 'surface integral on the boundary where T = 0'), OR integration over all space with decay faster than 1/r^3 (Pinto-Avelino eq.(25))
divergence-free alone is NOT sufficient (Wang secs.4-6: the field-only EM tensor of a charged sphere / finite electrostatic structure violates int T^{ij} = 0)
flat (Minkowski) spacetime / negligible self-gravity (Pinto-Avelino p.1, sec.III)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED in prose, KEPT in code -- the boundary condition. tolman.py:2622-2625 (PEER_STATUS 'this file's own reach') and tolman.py:1015-1017 say 'von Laue forces int_V T^i_i = 0 over a complete static bounded system, so 4 pi R^3 p_r(R) = 0 for ANY ball enclosing the whole device'. That needs T^{ij} n_j = 0 ON the enclosing sphere (compact support inside the ball), not merely a bounded DEVICE: a device's own static fields extend past it. Shown in rederive C3d: a bounded charged conducting shell, complete tensor (field + balancing wall tension) divergence-free everywhere, gives int_{ball R} T^ii = -Q^2/(8 pi eps0 R) != 0 for EVERY finite R > a; zero only as R -> infinity. The z3 layer does keep it: tolman.py:2387-2405 obligation L1 takes 'p_r = 0 at the cut' as its HYPOTHESIS (cited to Herrera's matching condition) and DRIFT L2 shows it is load-bearing -- so the drift is prose-only.

ATTRIBUTION (a discrepancy, not an error): tolman.py:129-139 calls 'the volume integral of the spatial stress is a surface term' von Laue's theorem 'in its finite-volume form: Wang eq.(20)'. In Wang, eq.(20) is his own sec.6 Gauss-law identity used to relate divergence to the theorem's condition; von Laue's theorem proper (Wang sec.2) is the four-vector criterion with int Theta^{ij} = 0 as its CONDITION, and per Wang fn.7 Laue proved only its sufficiency. The restatements disagree on what Laue proved: Lorce et al. p.5 says 'von Laue [30] showed that Eq.(23) is a necessary and sufficient condition'. The usage 'von Laue condition' for int p = 0 (Lorce eq.(15), Pinto-Avelino eq.(27)) is conventional. Neither reading changes the mathematics the tree uses.

ADDED (over-restrictive, harmless direction): tolman.py:567 'Wang's eq.(20) needs the REGION to be a ball'. Eq.(20) holds for any region V with boundary S (Wang: 'The integral domain V can be multiply connected'); the ball is needed only for the surface term to reduce to 4 pi R^3 <T^{rr}>(R). The tree's use of a ball is correct; the stated necessity is attributed to eq.(20) rather than to the reduction.

KEPT: 'complete' (field plus mirrors) matches the published requirement that the TOTAL tensor be divergence-free; Wang secs.4-5 and rederive C4 show the field-only tensor fails (int T^ii = Q^2/(8 pi eps0 a) over all space). tolman.py:2608 'for a COMPLETE apparatus' is right to insist on it.
KEPT: flat space (tolman.py:129 'Strip gravity'); Sorge 2011.10991 eq.(36) extends the vanishing to O(gamma) weak field with sqrt(-g), under the same compact-support assumption (a).

CITATION DISCREPANCY, as the tree already records (tolman.py:151-157): Wang prints 'Ann. Phys. 35, 524 (1911)'; Lorce et al. and Pinto & Avelino both print 'Annalen (der) Phys(ik) 340, 524 (1911)'. Two independent restatements now carry 340, so both numberings are in print for the same page. The tree's issue number '(8)' is printed by none of the four sources read here -- unverified, not contradicted.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (15 checks, ~12 s). C1: the product-rule identity under Wang eq.(20) holds symbolically for an arbitrary static tensor, every i, mu. C2: for a divergence-free, NON-spherical, compactly supported stress T^{ij} = delta_ij Lap(phi) - d_i d_j phi (phi = (1-r^2)^4 (1 + xz + y^2/3)), int_{ball R} T^ii == R^3 oint n_i n_j T^{ij} dOmega = 4 pi R^3 <T^rr> exactly (sympy residual 0); it is -435 pi/128 != 0 at R = 1/2 (inside the support) and exactly 0 at R = 1 (support boundary) -- the vanishing form holds under compact support. C3: bounded charged conducting shell with balancing surface tension (complete tensor conserved everywhere): int_{ball R>a} T^ii = 4 pi R^3 p_r(R) = -Q^2/(8 pi eps0 R) != 0 for every finite R, -> 0 as R -> infinity; contrast +Q/-Q concentric shells (field confined, compact T) give exactly 0 for R > b; the finite-ball deviation obeys Pinto-Avelino's bound |int_ball p| <= m_out with ratio exactly 1/3 (w = 1/3 for EM). C4: field-only tensor over all space gives Q^2/(8 pi eps0 a) != 0 (Wang secs.4-5 reproduced). C5 (z3 5.1.0): identity + p_r = 0 at cut => m = 0 (negation unsat); p_r free => m = 0 not forced (sat); vacuity guard sat -- the tree's L1 logic reproduced.

later_literature.what: Divergence-free alone is neither necessary nor sufficient for int Theta^{ij} = 0; divergence-free PLUS the boundary condition oint dS_l Theta^{l mu} X^i = 0 (true if Theta = 0 on the boundary) is sufficient. Counterexamples: charged metal sphere, finite electrostatic equilibrium structure (field-only tensor). Also claims the Landau-Lifshitz and Weinberg versions of the four-vector theorem are flawed -- a claim about the four-vector theorem, not the part the tree uses.

QFT version: for a closed system in a normalizable stationary state, sum_i <int T^ii> = 0 (eq.14) and the tensor form <int T^ij> = 0 (eq.19), surface terms dropped by assumption; with external force int T^ij = -int x^i F^j (eq.18); M = <int T^mu_mu> (eq.65). Attributes the SNC to von Laue, disagreeing with Wang fn.7 on what Laue proved.

Casimir apparatus in a weak field: int sqrt(-g) T^i_(C)i = 0 (eq.36) under assumption (a) T vanishing outside the domain and eq.(35)'s surface term on the boundary where T = 0; ideal plates with edge effects neglected (L << sqrt(A)); attributes the cancellation to the virial theorem.

later_literature.ref: S. R. Pinto & P. P. Avelino, arXiv:2502.10427v2 (2025), 'Deviations from the von Laue condition'
later_literature.what: States the condition with the explicit alternative hypothesis T = 0 at the boundary OR whole space with decay faster than 1/r^3 (eq.25); shows that over a FINITE ball the integrated pressure deviates from zero, bounded by the energy outside the ball under the DEC, |int_0^r p| <= m_out (eqs.39-43); 'it does not generally hold when interactions extend beyond a particle's characteristic size'. This is exactly the class the tree's 'ANY ball enclosing the whole device' sentence drops; reproduced in rederive C3h.

lacked_data: What von Laue (1911) lacked: general relativity (1915), quantum field theory and renormalised vacuum stress (the Casimir effect, 1948), and the measured pressure distributions of hadrons (gravitational form factors, 2018 onward). Does having them change the conclusion? The evidence read here says no, in either direction. (i) The finite-volume relation is an identity (the product rule plus Gauss) with no empirical input, re-derived here symbolically (C1, C2). (ii) The vanishing form carries over to QFT expectation values in stationary normalizable states (Lorce et al. eqs.14, 19, with surface terms dropped by assumption) and to a Casimir apparatus at O(gamma) in a weak field (Sorge eq.36, compact support assumed). No refutation was found in the literature read, and none was constructed. (iii) The one limit the later work makes explicit is not new data but a hypothesis that was always needed: the boundary term must vanish (Moller's zero-boundary condition, 1955, as reported by Wang; Pinto-Avelino eq.25). Pinto & Avelino 2025 quantify how far the condition fails on a finite ball when fields extend past it. Hadron data do not test von Laue: the proton D-term analyses impose the condition rather than measure it (Pinto-Avelino p.5 describe the proton pressure as satisfying it). NOT checked here: whether any measurement has been independent of the condition. M's hypothesis is therefore NOT supported for this result, and no datum has moved.
grade_evidence: The identity the tree cites (Wang eq.(20); the volume integral of the spatial stress equals a surface term) is re-derived exactly: C1 symbolically, and C2 with sympy residual 0 on a non-spherical conserved stress. Its sign and direction as the tree now states them (the surface term on the left, equal to 4 pi R^3 <T^rr>) are confirmed. The vanishing form holds on a smaller class than tolman.py:2622-2625 and 1015-1017 state. It needs T = 0 on the enclosing sphere (compact support), which Wang, Sorge and Pinto-Avelino all state explicitly. 'A complete static bounded system' is not enough when the device's fields extend past it. The counterexample is shown in rederive C3d: a bounded device with a conserved complete tensor gives int_{ball R} T^ii = -Q^2/(8 pi eps0 R) != 0 on every finite enclosing ball. Pinto & Avelino 2025 bound the same deviation in general (reproduced exactly, C3h). The tree's code already carries the hypothesis: z3 L1 at tolman.py:2387-2405 takes p_r = 0 at the cut as a premise, and DRIFT L2 proves the premise load-bearing. So the narrowing affects prose only and moves no verdict. The refusal 'ball_excludes_walls' is conservative under the narrower class: on a non-compact device it refuses where the test could have had content, and it never reports a false zero. What the tree's sentence should carry is the named hypothesis 'T^{ij} n_j = 0 on the sphere (compact support inside the ball)'. The attribution of eq.(20) to von Laue, the 35-versus-340 volume number, and 'eq.(20) needs a ball' are discrepancies, not refutations. Graded NARROWED, not STANDS, because the tree's printed statement drops a hypothesis the source requires and a counterexample to that statement is computed here. Not WRONG, because the result as the tree actually applies it (L1, with p_r = 0 at the cut) is correct.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: rephrase tolman.py:1015-1017 and 2622-2625 as '4 pi R^3 p_r(R) = 0 for any ball whose boundary lies outside the support of the complete T' (or define 'bounded system' as compact support of T), so that prose and code match. That is a change to the tree, which this audit does not make. To OPEN on the attribution point only: reading von Laue 1911 at source, which is not possible here (no arXiv copy), would settle whether Laue stated sufficiency only (Wang fn.7) or the SNC (Lorce et al. p.5). Neither outcome touches the mathematics. To WRONG: only an application of the vanishing form to a tensor that is not compactly supported inside the ball. None was found. L1's premise and the pointwise_test refusal both avoid it.
